mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: For statements like "The number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have", interpret as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement equates a "has more than" difference to another difference.
mathgap.example: Treating the equation as |A - B| = |C - D| (ignoring sign) leads to an incorrect solution.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations, simplify them, and propagate the information to solve for other variables.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After any variable is assigned a concrete value, update all equations that involve it.
mathgap.example: Failing to substitute a known value into other equations, leaving the system underdetermined.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative and difference statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, respecting the order of statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing statements that refer to counts after earlier transfers or updates.
mathgap.example: Applying a comparison based on a person's initial count, ignoring a prior transfer that changed it.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the subset of equations and statements that involve the queried person directly or through other variables, and focus solving effort on that subsystem.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem asks for a specific person's count and many statements are irrelevant.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations, including unrelated variables, leading to unnecessary complexity.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating them.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever multiple similar‑sounding names appear in the problem.
mathgap.example: Confusing "Kaylyn" with "Kendra" and merging their counts.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When parsing a phrase like "the difference between the number of items that A and B have", keep the order of A and B as given, interpreting it as (A - B).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement mentions "difference between" without specifying "more" or "fewer".
mathgap.example: Treating "difference between A and B" as an absolute value, losing the sign.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative statements of the form "A has K more than B" as A - B = K, and "A has K fewer than B" as A - B = -K, preserving the order of names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing any comparative statement that uses the words "more" or "fewer".
mathgap.example: Incorrectly treating "A has 5 fewer carrots than B" as A - B = 5, leading to a sign error.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X has N items", set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value; later statements can update it again. This resolves contradictory direct‑count statements by using the most recent one.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct‑count statement, especially if the same person appears in multiple such statements.
mathgap.example: Treating both "Roseann has 50 pears" and "Roseann has 6 pears" as simultaneous constraints, causing inconsistency, instead of using the later value.

mathgap.title: Transfer, Split, Redistribution, Conditional Transfer Handling
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X gives N items to Y" as subtract N from X and add N to Y. Interpret "X splits all the items she owns equally among Y and Z" as X gives all items away, each receiving half (X becomes 0). Interpret "X and Y redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount" as combine X+Y and set each to half the total. Interpret conditional transfers like "If X has more than Y items, X will transfer their items to Z" by evaluating the condition at that point and moving all of X's items to Z if true.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing any transfer, split, redistribution, or conditional‑transfer statement.
mathgap.example: Misreading "Taylor splits all the pears she owns equally among Nealie and Schuyler" as a simple fixed‑amount transfer, rather than giving all pears away and dividing them.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative Increase Handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "The number of items that X has increases by N times" (including fractional N), interpret it as X's new count = X's current count * (1 + N). For example, "increase by 2 times" means X becomes three times its previous amount.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing statements about multiplicative increases.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "The number of pears that Rollin has increases by 2 times" as doubling instead of tripling, leading to an incorrect final count.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than"
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets "A has K more than B" as B - A = K, reversing the intended subtraction.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map "A has K more than B" to A - B = K, preserving the order of names.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign when interpreting difference statements, assuming they are always positive.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Keep the signed difference; do not take the absolute value.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies all transfers as if they occurred simultaneously, ignoring the narrative order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfer statements sequentially in the order they appear.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes a direct‑count statement sets a permanent initial value, not updating it later.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat each "has N" statement as setting the count at that point, overriding any previous value.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses "increase by N times" with either simple multiplication by N or adding N, ignoring the correct (1+N) factor.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a statement says "increase by N times", compute new = old * (1 + N). For fractional N, use rational arithmetic.
